agency_phone_invalid.title: Check the agency's public phone number
agency_phone_invalid.meaning: The agency phone number did not pass an optional Google compatibility check.
agency_phone_invalid.impact: Passengers may not be able to contact the operator using this number.
fix_steps: Check `agency_phone` in `agency.txt` against the operator's published contact details.
Correct the number and country code if needed. If it is valid, review the compatibility check before changing it.
agency_phone_invalid.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

attribution_without_role.title: An attribution does not say what the organization does
attribution_without_role.meaning: An attribution row has no role set to `1`.
attribution_without_role.impact: Users of the feed cannot tell whether this organization produced the data, operates the service, or acts as the authority.
fix_steps: Find the reported row in `attributions.txt`.
Set at least one of `is_producer`, `is_operator`, or `is_authority` to `1`, according to the organization's actual role.
attribution_without_role.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

bidirectional_exit_gate.title: An exit-only gate allows travel in both directions
bidirectional_exit_gate.meaning: A pathway has `pathway_mode=7` and is marked as bidirectional.
bidirectional_exit_gate.impact: A journey planner may suggest entering through an exit-only gate.
fix_steps: Find the reported row in `pathways.txt`.
For a real exit-only gate, set `is_bidirectional=0` and check the direction from `from_stop_id` to `to_stop_id`. If the gate serves a different purpose, correct its mode instead.
bidirectional_exit_gate.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

big_gap_in_service.title: A service has a gap of at least 14 days
big_gap_in_service.meaning: The calendar for the reported `serviceId` has a long break between active dates.
big_gap_in_service.impact: This may be an intentional seasonal break or a missing part of the timetable.
fix_steps: Check the reported gap against `calendar.txt` and the added or removed dates in `calendar_dates.txt`.
Restore missing service dates if the service should run. Keep an intentional break; do not add departures that are not operated.
big_gap_in_service.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

block_trips_with_overlapping_stop_times.title: One vehicle is assigned to overlapping trips
block_trips_with_overlapping_stop_times.meaning: Two trips share a `block_id` and overlap on a date when both services operate.
block_trips_with_overlapping_stop_times.impact: The block cannot describe a single vehicle's actual work, and stay-on-board connections may be misleading.
fix_steps: Use `tripIdA`, `tripIdB`, and `intersection` to compare both trips' stop times on the reported service date.
Correct an erroneous time or calendar, or assign the trips to their actual vehicle blocks. Do not change a real departure simply to remove the overlap.
block_trips_with_overlapping_stop_times.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

csv_parsing_failed.title: A file could not be read as CSV
csv_parsing_failed.meaning: The CSV reader could not parse the reported file. The message and position identify where reading failed.
csv_parsing_failed.impact: Some or all of the file may be unavailable to later checks, so the report may be incomplete.
fix_steps: Open `filename` and inspect the parser's `message`, `lineIndex`, and nearby text. Check delimiters and balanced quotes.
Export comma-separated UTF-8 CSV. Quote values containing commas and double any literal quote inside a quoted value; remove unintended line breaks from GTFS field values.
csv_parsing_failed.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

decreasing_or_equal_stop_time_distance.title: Distance does not increase between stops
decreasing_or_equal_stop_time_distance.meaning: Within a trip, `shape_dist_traveled` stays the same or decreases as `stop_sequence` increases.
decreasing_or_equal_stop_time_distance.impact: The distances can place stops on the wrong part of the trip's shape, especially on loops.
fix_steps: Compare the reported row with `prevCsvRowNumber` in `stop_times.txt` and check the actual stop order.
Recalculate cumulative distances along the correct shape, using the same units as `shapes.txt`. Preserve enough precision for consecutive values to increase; do not invent increments.
decreasing_or_equal_stop_time_distance.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

decreasing_shape_distance.title: Distance goes backwards along a shape
decreasing_shape_distance.meaning: A later shape point has a smaller `shape_dist_traveled` value than the previous point.
decreasing_shape_distance.impact: Apps cannot reliably use these distances to place stops along the route line.
fix_steps: Sort the reported shape by `shape_pt_sequence` and inspect both reported rows in `shapes.txt`.
Correct the point order or recalculate cumulative distances from the start of the shape. Keep the units consistent with `stop_times.txt`.
decreasing_shape_distance.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

duplicate_fare_media.title: Two fare media have the same name and type
duplicate_fare_media.meaning: Different `fare_media_id` values describe the same combination of `fare_media_name` and `fare_media_type`.
duplicate_fare_media.impact: The records may be duplicates, making fare products harder to maintain and identify.
fix_steps: Compare the two reported rows in `fare_media.txt` and their references in `fare_products.txt`.
If they describe one medium, keep one ID and update its references. If they are distinct, use their actual distinguishing names or types.
duplicate_fare_media.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

duplicate_geo_json_key.title: Two geographic features use the same ID
duplicate_geo_json_key.meaning: More than one feature in `locations.geojson` uses the reported feature ID.
duplicate_geo_json_key.impact: A `location_id` reference cannot identify a single service area reliably.
fix_steps: Compare the features at `firstIndex` and `secondIndex`.
Remove an accidental duplicate or assign unique IDs to distinct areas. Update the corresponding `location_id` references in `stop_times.txt`.
duplicate_geo_json_key.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

duplicate_geography_id.title: An ID is shared by different location types
duplicate_geography_id.meaning: The same ID appears in more than one of `stops.txt`, `location_groups.txt`, and `locations.geojson`.
duplicate_geography_id.impact: The ID does not uniquely identify a stop, group, or service area.
fix_steps: Find `geographyId` in all three sources and identify which locations are intended.
Assign distinct IDs and update references in `stop_times.txt` and, where applicable, `location_group_stops.txt`.
duplicate_geography_id.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

duplicate_key.title: Two rows have the same unique key
duplicate_key.meaning: The reported rows have an identical ID or identical combination of key fields.
duplicate_key.impact: An app may reject the records or choose a row unpredictably.
fix_steps: Compare `oldCsvRowNumber` and `newCsvRowNumber` in `filename`, using the reported key fields.
Remove a true duplicate. For different entities, correct the key and update affected references. For a compound key, such as `trip_id` plus `stop_sequence`, check the whole combination.
duplicate_key.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

duplicate_route_name.title: Two routes have indistinguishable names
duplicate_route_name.meaning: Routes for the same agency and transport type share the same short-name and long-name combination.
duplicate_route_name.impact: Passengers may have difficulty choosing the intended route.
fix_steps: Compare the reported routes with the operator's public route names.

Merge accidental duplicates and update trips, or use genuinely distinct public names. Opposite directions normally belong to one route. Keep legitimate identical names when the real services require them.
duplicate_route_name.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

duplicate_trip.title: Two records describe the same scheduled trip
duplicate_trip.meaning: An optional Google compatibility check found matching route, service, and stop-time information for multiple trips.
duplicate_trip.impact: An app may display duplicate departures.
fix_steps: Compare the trips and check whether both vehicles really operate.
Remove an accidental duplicate and update its references, or correct the attributes that should distinguish the trips. Preserve genuine simultaneous services.
duplicate_trip.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

duplicated_column.title: A column name appears twice
duplicated_column.meaning: The header row contains the same field name more than once.
duplicated_column.impact: A reader cannot reliably determine which column supplies that field's value.
fix_steps: Open the header of the reported `filename` and compare the columns at `firstIndex` and `secondIndex`.
Merge or remove an accidental duplicate column, or give a mislabeled column its correct GTFS name. Keep every data row aligned with the header.
duplicated_column.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

empty_column_name.title: A column has no name
empty_column_name.meaning: At least one header cell is empty, often because of an extra comma.
empty_column_name.impact: The validator skips the unnamed column, which may hide intended data.
fix_steps: Check the header position identified by `index` and the values beneath it.
Name a real field correctly, or remove the unused column from both the header and every data row.
empty_column_name.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

empty_file.title: A GTFS file has no usable content
empty_file.meaning: The file has no header, or a required file has no data rows.
empty_file.impact: Required information may be missing, preventing the feed from loading correctly.
fix_steps: Open the reported file and check whether the export produced a header and records.
Regenerate the missing content from the source. Remove an optional empty file only if no feature or reference requires it.
empty_file.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

empty_row.title: A file contains a blank row
empty_row.meaning: The reported CSV row contains no meaningful values.
empty_row.impact: Some CSV readers may treat it as a malformed record instead of skipping it.
fix_steps: Find the reported row in `filename`.
Remove the blank or whitespace-only record and adjust the export so it does not produce extra records.
empty_row.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates.title: Different shape points have the same distance
equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates.meaning: Two consecutive shape points have equal cumulative distances even though their coordinates are separated beyond the rule's tolerance.
equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates.impact: The distance values do not describe the geometry, so stop-to-shape matching may be wrong.
fix_steps: Compare the reported points in `shapes.txt`, ordered by `shape_pt_sequence`.
Correct an erroneous coordinate or recompute cumulative distances with adequate precision. Do not move a correct point merely to match a wrong distance.
equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates_di.title: Nearby shape points share a rounded distance
equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates_di.meaning: Consecutive points have different coordinates but equal cumulative distances, with a small geographic separation.
equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates_di.impact: Rounding may make it difficult to interpolate accurately between the points.
fix_steps: Check the coordinates and distance precision in the two reported `shapes.txt` rows.
Recalculate distances with enough decimal places, or remove a redundant point if doing so preserves the actual path.
equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates_di.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

equal_shape_distance_same_coordinates.title: A shape repeats the same point and distance
equal_shape_distance_same_coordinates.meaning: Consecutive rows of one shape have identical coordinates and `shape_dist_traveled` values.
equal_shape_distance_same_coordinates.impact: The repeated point adds no travel information and may complicate shape processing.
fix_steps: Compare the reported consecutive rows in `shapes.txt`.
Remove an accidental repeated point and preserve the remaining order. Do not remove later visits to the same place on a real loop.
equal_shape_distance_same_coordinates.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

expired_calendar.title: A service's active dates have ended
expired_calendar.meaning: The reported service has no remaining active dates after considering both the weekly calendar and date exceptions.
expired_calendar.impact: Trips using this service will not provide upcoming departures.
fix_steps: Check the service in both `calendar.txt` and `calendar_dates.txt` against the intended publication period.
Publish the confirmed new timetable, or remove retired service records and their dependent trips. Do not extend dates without confirming that the service still runs.
expired_calendar.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

fare_product_with_multiple_default_rider.title: A fare product has more than one default rider category
fare_product_with_multiple_default_rider.meaning: The same fare product is linked to multiple categories marked as default.
fare_product_with_multiple_default_rider.impact: An app cannot select a single default fare category reliably.
fix_steps: Find the reported product in `fare_products.txt` and inspect its categories in `rider_categories.txt`.
Correct the product links or default flags so that each product has at most one default category. Check other products before changing a shared category.
fare_product_with_multiple_default_rider.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

fare_transfer_rule_duration_limit_type_w.title: A transfer time limit has no duration
fare_transfer_rule_duration_limit_type_w.impact: The fare rule says how to measure a time limit without saying how long it is.
fix_steps: Find the reported row in `fare_transfer_rules.txt`.
Add the actual limit in seconds, or clear the limit type if this rule has no time limit.
fare_transfer_rule_duration_limit_type_w.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

fare_transfer_rule_duration_limit_withou.title: A transfer duration does not say how to measure it
fare_transfer_rule_duration_limit_withou.impact: An app cannot tell which events start and end the transfer time limit.
fix_steps: Check the ticket's actual transfer policy.
Set `duration_limit_type` to the matching GTFS value, or clear the duration if no limit applies.
fare_transfer_rule_duration_limit_withou.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

fare_transfer_rule_invalid_transfer_coun.title: The allowed transfer count is invalid
fare_transfer_rule_invalid_transfer_coun.meaning: The reported `transfer_count` is zero or less than `-1` where a count is required.
fare_transfer_rule_invalid_transfer_coun.impact: The rule cannot express a valid allowance for repeated transfers within a leg group.
fix_steps: Check the row in `fare_transfer_rules.txt` against the fare policy.
Use a positive integer for a limited number of transfers or `-1` for unlimited transfers. Do not use zero as a substitute for an unknown value.
fare_transfer_rule_invalid_transfer_coun.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

fare_transfer_rule_with_forbidden_transf.title: A transfer count is set where it is not allowed
fare_transfer_rule_with_forbidden_transf.meaning: `transfer_count` is populated without matching, defined from/to leg-group IDs.
fare_transfer_rule_with_forbidden_transf.impact: This combines a transfer-count condition with a rule that does not support it.
fix_steps: Check `from_leg_group_id` and `to_leg_group_id` in the reported row.
Clear `transfer_count` for a rule between different leg groups. If the rule is actually within one group, correct both IDs to that group and supply its real allowance.
fare_transfer_rule_with_forbidden_transf.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

fare_transfer_rule_without_transfer_coun.title: A within-group transfer rule has no transfer count
fare_transfer_rule_without_transfer_coun.meaning: The from/to leg-group IDs are equal, but `transfer_count` is empty.
fare_transfer_rule_without_transfer_coun.impact: An app cannot tell how many transfers the rule permits.
fix_steps: Find the reported row in `fare_transfer_rules.txt` and confirm the leg-group IDs.
Set the actual positive transfer count, or `-1` if unlimited. If the IDs are wrong, correct the groups first.
fare_transfer_rule_without_transfer_coun.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

fast_travel_between_consecutive_stops.title: Travel between two stops appears too fast
fast_travel_between_consecutive_stops.meaning: The distance and elapsed time between consecutive stops imply a speed above the rule's threshold for this transport type.
fast_travel_between_consecutive_stops.impact: A wrong stop location or time can produce misleading journey durations.
fix_steps: Compare the reported stop IDs, coordinates, departure time, arrival time, and `speedKph` with the actual journey.
Correct the mistaken coordinate, stop reference, time, or route type. For travel after midnight, preserve the service-day time, such as `25:10:00`. Keep verified unusual services unchanged.
fast_travel_between_consecutive_stops.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

fast_travel_between_far_stops.title: Travel between distant stops appears too fast
fast_travel_between_far_stops.meaning: Two stops more than 10 km apart imply a speed above the threshold for the route's transport type.
fast_travel_between_far_stops.impact: A distant wrong stop or missing hour can distort the trip's journey time substantially.
fix_steps: Use the reported IDs, distance, times, and speed to inspect the pair on a map and in the timetable.
Correct wrong references, coordinates, times, or route type. Check the service-day date before changing an overnight journey.
fast_travel_between_far_stops.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

feed_expiration_date30_days.title: The feed has less than a month of validity left
feed_expiration_date30_days.meaning: The feed's declared end date does not provide the recommended 30-day planning horizon.
feed_expiration_date30_days.impact: Passengers planning ahead may soon run out of published timetable information.
fix_steps: Compare `feed_end_date` with the actual service coverage in both calendar files.
Publish confirmed service dates for the next period and update `feed_info.txt` to match. Do not extend the metadata alone.
feed_expiration_date30_days.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

feed_expiration_date7_days.title: The feed expires within seven days
feed_expiration_date7_days.meaning: The declared `feed_end_date` is seven days away or sooner.
feed_expiration_date7_days.impact: Journey planners may soon have no current feed to use.
fix_steps: Check the reported end date and the operator's next confirmed timetable.
Publish an updated feed before the current one expires, with matching calendar coverage and feed dates.
feed_expiration_date7_days.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

feed_info_lang_and_agency_lang_mismatch.title: The feed and agency languages do not agree
feed_info_lang_and_agency_lang_mismatch.meaning: `feed_lang` does not match the agency language information under this check's language rules.
feed_info_lang_and_agency_lang_mismatch.impact: Apps may choose inappropriate pronunciation or language handling for passenger text.
fix_steps: Compare `feed_lang` with every `agency_lang` and the actual language of the source text.
Correct erroneous language tags. Use `mul` only when the feed's original text is genuinely multilingual; do not change tags just to make them equal.
feed_info_lang_and_agency_lang_mismatch.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

feed_valid_beyond_total_service_window.title: Feed validity extends well beyond the service dates
feed_valid_beyond_total_service_window.meaning: The feed starts more than 14 days before its first service date or ends more than 14 days after its last service date.
feed_valid_beyond_total_service_window.impact: The declared validity period includes a long stretch without published service, so the feed may appear to cover dates for which it has no departures.
fix_steps: Compare the reported feed dates and service-window dates with both calendar files.
Add missing confirmed service, or shorten the validity period to match the data. Keep intentional gaps only after checking their purpose.
feed_valid_beyond_total_service_window.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

forbidden_arrival_or_departure_time.title: A stop-time row mixes fixed times and a service window
forbidden_arrival_or_departure_time.meaning: The same row contains arrival/departure times and a pickup/drop-off window.
forbidden_arrival_or_departure_time.impact: An app cannot consistently interpret the row as both a scheduled stop and a window-based service.
fix_steps: Inspect the reported row in `stop_times.txt` and confirm how the service actually operates.
For a window-based row, clear fixed arrival/departure times. For a scheduled stop, remove the window fields and supply the required fixed times.
forbidden_arrival_or_departure_time.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

forbidden_continuous_pickup_drop_off.title: Route-wide continuous service conflicts with a pickup window
forbidden_continuous_pickup_drop_off.meaning: A route allows continuous pickup or drop-off while one of its trips uses pickup/drop-off windows.
forbidden_continuous_pickup_drop_off.impact: These settings combine incompatible ways of describing passenger access.
fix_steps: Inspect the reported route and stop-time rows.

For a window-based service, use route settings that do not declare continuous pickup/drop-off, as required by the specification. Otherwise remove incorrectly exported windows and model the actual service.
forbidden_continuous_pickup_drop_off.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

forbidden_drop_off_type.title: Scheduled drop-off conflicts with a service window
forbidden_drop_off_type.meaning: A pickup/drop-off window is present alongside `drop_off_type=0`, including an applicable default.
forbidden_drop_off_type.impact: The row mixes a flexible service window with regularly scheduled drop-off.
fix_steps: Check the reported row in `stop_times.txt` and the actual drop-off arrangement.
For a window-based service, choose an allowed drop-off type that matches the service. If drop-off is scheduled, remove the inappropriate window and provide the required times.
forbidden_drop_off_type.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

forbidden_geography_id.title: A stop-time row identifies more than one location
forbidden_geography_id.meaning: More than one of `stop_id`, `location_group_id`, and `location_id` is filled in.
forbidden_geography_id.impact: The row does not identify a single kind of boarding or alighting location.
fix_steps: Determine whether the row serves a specific stop, a group of stops, or a geographic area.
Keep only the corresponding location field and verify that its ID exists in the correct source.
forbidden_geography_id.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

forbidden_pickup_type.title: The pickup type conflicts with a service window
forbidden_pickup_type.meaning: A pickup/drop-off window is used with a pickup type that this rule forbids: regularly scheduled pickup or coordination directly with the driver.
forbidden_pickup_type.impact: The row gives contradictory instructions about how pickup works.
fix_steps: Check `pickup_type` and both window fields in the reported `stop_times.txt` row.
Choose a permitted pickup type that reflects the real window-based service, or remove incorrectly exported windows for a scheduled service.
forbidden_pickup_type.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

forbidden_prior_day_booking_field_value.title: An advance-booking rule contains incompatible fields
forbidden_prior_day_booking_field_value.meaning: A prior-day booking rule includes fields that are not permitted for that booking type.
forbidden_prior_day_booking_field_value.impact: Apps cannot interpret the booking deadline consistently.
fix_steps: Use `bookingRuleId`, `csvRowNumber`, and `fieldNames` to locate the conflicting values in `booking_rules.txt`.
If prior-day booking is correct, clear the reported forbidden fields and retain its required day/time deadline. Otherwise correct `booking_type` and its dependent fields together.
forbidden_prior_day_booking_field_value.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

forbidden_prior_notice_start_day.title: Two alternative booking-window limits are both set
forbidden_prior_notice_start_day.impact: The rule expresses the booking window using incompatible alternatives.
fix_steps: Check the actual opening time for bookings.
Keep the applicable day-based or duration-based limit, clear the incompatible field, and review any dependent time fields.
forbidden_prior_notice_start_day.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

forbidden_prior_notice_start_time.title: A booking start time has no start day
forbidden_prior_notice_start_time.impact: The time alone does not identify when advance booking opens.

Correct spelling and use the GTFS table name without the `.txt` extension. Restore a required target file or remove an obsolete translation; check support before retaining an extension.
translation_unknown_table_name.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

trip_coverage_not_active_for_next7_days.title: The main timetable coverage ends within seven days
trip_coverage_not_active_for_next7_days.meaning: The validator's window of substantial trip activity ends too soon.
trip_coverage_not_active_for_next7_days.impact: A small amount of later service may remain while most passengers lose upcoming departures.
fix_steps: Compare the reported service window with the next confirmed timetable, including trips and both calendar files.
Publish the missing upcoming service and align feed metadata with it. Extending `feed_end_date` alone does not extend trip coverage.
trip_coverage_not_active_for_next7_days.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance.title: The last stop's distance goes beyond the shape
trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance.meaning: The trip's final `shape_dist_traveled` exceeds the shape's maximum distance, and the endpoint separation exceeds the implementation's 11.1 m threshold.
trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance.impact: The stop distances and route geometry do not describe the same endpoint reliably.
fix_steps: Compare `maxTripDistanceTraveled`, `maxShapeDistanceTraveled`, the units, and the reported endpoint separation.
Correct the trip's shape assignment, extend an incomplete shape to the real endpoint, or recompute distances from accurate geometry. Do not just increase the shape's final number.
trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance_bel.title: The stop distance exceeds the shape despite nearby endpoints
trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance_bel.meaning: The final stop's cumulative distance exceeds the shape's maximum, but the endpoints are within the implementation's 11.1 m tolerance.
trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance_bel.impact: Rounding or inconsistent distance calculations may prevent reliable stop placement.
fix_steps: Compare the maximum distance values, units, and endpoint coordinates in the reported trip and shape.
Recalculate with a shared distance origin and sufficient precision. Preserve the real geometry rather than shifting coordinates to match a rounded number.
trip_distance_exceeds_shape_distance_bel.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

trip_headsign_matches_intermediate_stop.title: The destination display names an intermediate stop
trip_headsign_matches_intermediate_stop.meaning: `trip_headsign` matches a stop before the trip's last stop.
trip_headsign_matches_intermediate_stop.impact: Passengers boarding later may see a destination the vehicle has already passed.
fix_steps: Compare the headsign with the actual vehicle display and the complete stop sequence.

Correct a mistaken trip headsign. If the display legitimately changes during the trip, represent the changes with appropriate `stop_headsign` values; do not assume every headsign must equal the final stop name.
trip_headsign_matches_intermediate_stop.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

trip_with_shape_dist_traveled_but_no_sha.title: Stop distances have no complete matching distances on the shape
trip_with_shape_dist_traveled_but_no_sha.meaning: A trip supplies `shape_dist_traveled` in `stop_times.txt`, but its shape lacks distances on some or all points.
trip_with_shape_dist_traveled_but_no_sha.impact: Apps cannot reliably locate those stop distances on the route geometry.
fix_steps: Find the trip's `shape_id` and inspect every point in `shapes.txt`; the report may identify only a representative stop-time row.
Populate consistent cumulative distances for all shape points using the same units and origin as the stop times. Recalculate both sides when needed.
trip_with_shape_dist_traveled_but_no_sha.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

u_r_i_syntax_error.title: A resource address cannot be read as a URI
u_r_i_syntax_error.meaning: A supplied address has invalid URI syntax.
u_r_i_syntax_error.impact: The validator may be unable to open the intended resource.
fix_steps: Read `exception` and `message` to identify the address and whether it came from the input source or another resource.
Correct malformed characters or use a supported local path or URL for that input. Do not edit unrelated GTFS rows when the failure concerns the archive address.
u_r_i_syntax_error.verification: Run validation again and confirm that it completes, including the previously failed stage. Review the complete report; an interrupted check does not establish that the feed is valid.

unexpected_enum_value.title: A coded field contains an unrecognized value
unexpected_enum_value.meaning: The value is not among the options recognized for this field by the validator.
unexpected_enum_value.impact: The setting may be ignored or interpreted differently by target apps.
fix_steps: Check the field's allowed values and the validator's supported specification version.
Correct a mistaken value to the option that describes the real service. If it is a newer valid option, update the validator and check consumer support instead of replacing it arbitrarily.
unexpected_enum_value.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unknown_column.title: A column name is not recognized
unknown_column.meaning: The file contains a column outside the validator's recognized schema.
unknown_column.impact: It may be an intentional extension or a typo that hides intended data.
fix_steps: Compare `fieldName` with the specification and your export configuration.
Correct a misspelling. Keep a documented extension when needed, and verify support in target apps; do not delete a newer standard field simply because an older validator does not recognize it.
unknown_column.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unknown_file.title: A file in the archive is not recognized
unknown_file.meaning: The archive contains a filename outside the validator's recognized GTFS files.
unknown_file.impact: The file may be ignored, or its name may hide data that should have been read.
fix_steps: Check the exact filename, extension, spelling, and purpose.
Rename a misnamed GTFS file correctly. Remove unrelated export artifacts when unnecessary; retain intentional extensions only with appropriate consumer support.
unknown_file.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unsorted_stop_times.title: Stop-time rows are not grouped and ordered by trip
unsorted_stop_times.meaning: Rows for a trip are not contiguous or do not appear in `stop_sequence` order.
unsorted_stop_times.impact: Some tools process grouped, ordered records more efficiently; the notice does not mean the service sequence itself is necessarily wrong.
fix_steps: Check whether the data is correct when grouped by `trip_id` and sorted numerically by `stop_sequence`.
Export in that order while keeping each row's values unchanged. Do not renumber a correct sequence merely to match an accidental file order.
unsorted_stop_times.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unsupported_feature_type.title: A GeoJSON item is not a Feature
unsupported_feature_type.meaning: An item in `locations.geojson` uses an unsupported feature type.
unsupported_feature_type.impact: The service-area item may not be read.
fix_steps: Find the item using `featureId` or `featureIndex`.
Represent the actual area as a GeoJSON `Feature` with the required ID, geometry, and properties. Do not relabel an incompatible object without restructuring it.
unsupported_feature_type.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unsupported_geo_json_type.title: The GeoJSON root is not a FeatureCollection
unsupported_geo_json_type.meaning: The top-level object in `locations.geojson` has an unsupported type.
unsupported_geo_json_type.impact: The validator cannot read the file as the required collection of service areas.
fix_steps: Inspect the root `type` and structure of `locations.geojson`.
Export a `FeatureCollection` containing a `features` array of valid service-area features, rather than changing only the type label.
unsupported_geo_json_type.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unsupported_geometry_type.title: A service area is not a Polygon or MultiPolygon
unsupported_geometry_type.meaning: A feature uses a geometry type that is not supported for GTFS service areas.
unsupported_geometry_type.impact: A point or line cannot define the required pickup/drop-off area.
fix_steps: Inspect the reported feature and its real service boundary.
Export that boundary as a valid `Polygon` or `MultiPolygon`. Use ordinary stops for point locations where appropriate; do not draw an arbitrary polygon around a bad feature.
unsupported_geometry_type.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unusable_trip.title: A trip has too few stops for a passenger journey
unusable_trip.meaning: The trip does not contain enough stop records to describe boarding and alighting.
unusable_trip.impact: Passengers cannot make a complete journey using the trip as exported.
fix_steps: Find the trip in `trips.txt` and inspect its records in `stop_times.txt`, including any omitted source data.
Restore the actual served sequence or remove a non-passenger/obsolete trip and its references. Do not add a dummy stop just to reach the minimum count.
unusable_trip.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unused_agency.title: No route refers to this agency
unused_agency.meaning: In a multi-agency feed, the reported agency is not used by `routes.agency_id` under the thorough check.
unused_agency.impact: The agency may be obsolete, or its routes may be missing or assigned incorrectly.
fix_steps: Compare the agency ID with route assignments and the intended export scope.
Restore missing routes or correct their agency references. Remove the agency only after checking other dependencies and confirming it is no longer needed.
unused_agency.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unused_parent_station.title: A station has no child locations
unused_parent_station.meaning: No location uses the station's ID in `parent_station`.
unused_parent_station.impact: Platforms or entrances may be missing from its hierarchy, or the station may be obsolete.
fix_steps: Search `stops.txt` for the station ID and inspect its expected platforms and entrances.
Add or correct genuine child relationships. Before deleting an obsolete station, check transfer and other references; do not create an imaginary platform.
unused_parent_station.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unused_route.title: A route has no trips
unused_route.meaning: The route exists in `routes.txt` but no trip references its ID.
unused_route.impact: Passengers cannot receive departures for this route from the feed.
fix_steps: Check the route's ID against `trips.txt` and the export's intended timetable period.
Restore missing trips or correct their route references. Remove a retired route only after reviewing fare, transfer, and other references.
unused_route.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unused_shape.title: No trip uses this route shape
unused_shape.meaning: A `shape_id` in `shapes.txt` is not referenced by any trip.
unused_shape.impact: The shape adds unused data and may indicate that a trip lost its geometry assignment.
fix_steps: Search `trips.shape_id` for the reported ID and compare with the intended journeys.
Restore missing shape references for real trips, or remove every point of a genuinely unused shape. Do not assign the shape to an unrelated trip.
unused_shape.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unused_station.title: A station has no child locations
unused_station.meaning: The station ID is not used as any location's `parent_station`.
unused_station.impact: The station hierarchy may be incomplete or left over from an older export.
fix_steps: Check the station's actual platforms and entrances, and compare their parent values.
Restore the real hierarchy or remove an obsolete station after checking other references. This code overlaps with `unused_parent_station`; it does not require a different physical repair.
unused_station.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unused_stop.title: A stop is not used by trips or their station hierarchy
unused_stop.meaning: The thorough check found no stop-time reference to this stop and no served descendant below it.
unused_stop.impact: The location may be obsolete, or a required relationship may be missing.
fix_steps: Check trip, station, pathway, and flexible-service references before deciding that the location is unnecessary.
Restore omitted references where the location is still used. Remove only genuinely obsolete data and update dependencies together.
unused_stop.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

unused_trip.title: A trip has no stop-time records
unused_trip.meaning: The trip exists in `trips.txt` but is not referenced in `stop_times.txt`.
unused_trip.impact: The feed cannot describe its passenger journey.
fix_steps: Search `stop_times.txt` for the exact `trip_id` and check the source export for missing records.
Restore the trip's real stop sequence, times, or flexible-service records. If the trip is obsolete, remove it and update any frequency or transfer references.
unused_trip.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.

wrong_parent_location_type.title: A location points to the wrong kind of parent
wrong_parent_location_type.meaning: The `parent_station` ID exists, but the parent's location type is not allowed for the child.
wrong_parent_location_type.impact: Apps cannot interpret the station hierarchy correctly.
fix_steps: Compare the child and parent rows named by the report.

Use a station (`1`) as parent for a platform, entrance, or generic node, and a platform (`0`) as parent for a boarding area. A station must have no parent. Correct the reference or a misclassified type to match the real location.
wrong_parent_location_type.verification: After a repair, rebuild the archive and validate it again. Confirm that the affected records are correct and that no new related notices appeared. A reviewed warning or informational notice may remain when it describes intentional, supported data.
